name: Great Panathenaia
description: Athens celebrates the birthday of Athena with grand processions, athletic games, and ritual sacrifices. Potters compete to create the finest prize amphorae.

name: Festival of Opet
description: The pharaoh processes from Karnak to Luxor as the Nile's flood brings renewal. Grain stores are opened and prices drop as Egypt celebrates abundance.

name: Isthmian Games
description: Athletes and spectators from across Greece gather at Corinth for the biennial games dedicated to Poseidon. Trade booms as visitors flood the isthmus.

name: Festival of Melqart
description: Tyre honors its patron god Melqart with sacred fires and ritual offerings. Merchants bring precious goods as temple dedications.

name: City Dionysia
description: The great dramatic festival of Athens, where playwrights compete with tragedies and comedies. Wine flows freely in honor of Dionysos.

name: Thesmophoria
description: Women celebrate the harvest festival of Demeter with secret rites. Grain offerings are central to the ceremony.

name: Navigium Isidis
description: The opening of the sailing season is celebrated with a grand procession to the harbor. A decorated ship is launched as an offering to Isis, protector of sailors.

name: Festival of Adonis
description: Byblos mourns and celebrates the death and rebirth of Adonis. Women plant 'Gardens of Adonis' and merchants bring offerings of spices and fine goods.

name: Saturnalia
description: Rome's great winter festival of gift-giving and feasting. Social rules are relaxed and the markets are filled with luxury goods.

name: Festival of Tanit
description: Carthage honors Tanit, goddess of fertility, with processions and offerings at the sacred tophet. Merchants bring their finest goods as dedications.

name: Karneia
description: Sparta's festival honoring Apollo Karneios. No military campaigns may be launched during the nine days of celebration. Trade in weapons and bronze slows.

name: Halieia
description: Rhodes celebrates its patron god Helios with athletic competitions and nautical races. Visitors arrive from across the Aegean, boosting local trade.
